title: Knowledge check: EDA with Base R and Tidyverse

questions.prompt: For “EDA with Base R and Tidyverse”, which approach best supports a reliable result?
options: Inspect assumptions, run a small example, and verify an edge case.
Trust the first output without inspecting its inputs.
Hide warnings and skip validation to make the result look clean.
Change several unrelated parts at once so the cause of any result is unclear.
questions.answer_key: Inspect assumptions, run a small example, and verify an edge case.
questions.explanation: EDA with Base R and Tidyverse is one step in Exploratory Data Analysis and Descriptive Statistics; exploratory data analysis generates questions and checks assumptions; descriptive summaries alone do not prove causality. Reliable work makes assumptions visible and checks behavior before scaling up.

questions.prompt: Which item is explicitly listed under “EDA with Base R and Tidyverse” in the source curriculum?
options: Change unrelated settings before checking the input
Assume one example proves every edge case
Skip validation when the output looks plausible
questions.explanation: The source PDF lists “Summary Functions” as part of lesson 136. The lesson retains the original topic wording.

questions.prompt: When applying “EDA with Base R and Tidyverse” to real work, what should you do before relying on the result?
options: Validate inputs and output shape, test a boundary case, and state limitations.
Assume missing and malformed inputs never occur.
Use the same method regardless of data type or the research question.
Remove inconvenient observations without recording the decision.
questions.answer_key: Validate inputs and output shape, test a boundary case, and state limitations.
questions.explanation: Use robust summaries and visual inspection, record exclusions, and keep the analysis reproducible. Record assumptions and known limitations instead of presenting a demonstration as proof.
